plan.title: Nine of twelve modules have a self-assessment gate with no answer key

narratives.Description: Four of the twelve core modules ship a self-assessment answer key, and the four that exist use three different headings, one of them an h3 nested under Acceptance evidence in the Lab 5 solution. Seven numbered self-assessment items across Modules 3, 4, and 6 carry no outcome id, so a learner cannot join an answer to the Completion-evidence row that scores it. The accepted design-critique remedy keeps Completion evidence as the scoring instrument and repairs findability and the outcome join rather than authoring eight new keys. Module 1 is excluded leftover: its self-assessment items are already tagged, but its Completion evidence carries no outcome-id rows and its scoring lives in an in-section block, so this change does not extend to it. Module 3 item 5 and Module 6 item 5 are resolved as ungraded practice rather than gaining a Completion-evidence row.
narratives.Overview:
> **Correction (author, during Module 5):** my first version of this issue said 3 keys exist and 9 are missing. That undercounted — my grep required the heading to begin with "Self-assessment", which missed Module 5's key at `### Module 5 self-assessment answers`. The accurate figure is **4 present, 8 missing**, and the table below is corrected. The finding stands; the *inconsistent heading and nesting* that hid Module 5's key from a reasonable search is now part of it.

## Situation

Every one of the twelve core modules ends with a **Self-assessment** section whose questions are explicitly outcome-mapped (e.g. Module 2 question 3 is tagged `O2.3`). The curriculum map states the completion rule plainly:

> A module is complete only when you can produce its stated evidence and answer its outcome-mapped self-assessment.

Only **four** modules ship an answer key. Eight do not.

| Module | Solution the module points to | Answer key |
|---|---|---|
| 01 | `solutions/module-01-what-directive-is.md` | ✅ `## Self-assessment key` |
| 02 | `solutions/lab-02-disposable-initialization.md` | ❌ |
| 03 | `solutions/module-03-authority-and-context.md` | ❌ |
| 04 | `solutions/module-04-xbrief-as-durable-state.md` | ✅ `## Self-assessment answers` |
| 05 | `solutions/lab-05-projection-drift-recovery.md` | ⚠️ `### Module 5 self-assessment answers` — present, but an `h3` nested under `## Acceptance evidence` |
| 06 | `solutions/module-06-creating-well-shaped-work.md` | ✅ `## Self-assessment answers` |
| 07 | `solutions/lab-07-scope-lifecycle.md` | ❌ |
| 08 | `solutions/module-08-session-and-work-selection.md` | ❌ |
| 09 | `solutions/module-09-design-critique-arcs.md` | ❌ |
| 10 | `solutions/lab-10-implementation-golden-path.md` | ❌ |
| 11 | `solutions/lab-11-testing-gates-and-evidence.md` | ❌ |
| 12 | `solutions/module-12-review-and-completion.md` | ❌ |

Reproduce:

```sh
grep -c '^## Self-assessment' curriculum/modules/*.md                        # 1 for all twelve
grep -rniE 'self-assessment (key|answers)' solutions/                        # only 01, 04, 05, 06
```

Three distinct headings are in use for the same artifact — `## Self-assessment key`, `## Self-assessment answers`, and `### Module 5 self-assessment answers`. There is no convention to search for.

## Pain experienced

I hit this at the end of Module 2. The module tells me to answer five questions and then says:

> **Demonstrated:** all five questions correctly demonstrate the four outcomes […] **Retry needed:** any answer depends only on memory […]

It then sends me to the "explained solution", which is `solutions/lab-02-disposable-initialization.md`. That file is thorough about the *lab* — install route, doctor warnings, the E401 decision drill, cleanup — but it never mentions the five self-assessment questions. So the module hands me a pass/retry gate and no way to evaluate it.

This is worse than simply having no self-assessment, for two reasons:

1. **Modules 1, 4, 5 and 6 set an expectation.** After Module 1 gave me a numbered key that corrected my reasoning, I read "use the explained solution to check your work" in later modules as the same promise. Discovering it is not is a trust problem, not just a gap.
2. **The course's own recovery ladder dead-ends.** `curriculum/README.md` prescribes: re-run the starting check → match expected failures → hints → "After a genuine first attempt, compare with the explained solution." For a self-assessment miss in eight of twelve modules, step 4 does not exist. The root README says the remaining move is to file a curriculum defect — which is what this is.

The practical effect for a self-directed learner: on questions where I *am* confident, the missing key costs nothing. On exactly the questions where I am not — the ones the self-assessment exists to catch — I have no way to tell a correct answer from a confident wrong one, and no instructor to ask. That inverts the purpose of the section. For a mid-level engineer new to Directive, the highest-risk misconceptions (active scope vs. present mutation permission; tracked vs. authoritative; implemented vs. delivered) are precisely the ones these questions probe.

It also makes the module-completion rule unenforceable. I can produce the lab evidence, but I cannot honestly certify the second half of the completion condition, so I cannot tell whether I am ready for the next module or carrying a silent misunderstanding into it.

**The inconsistent heading has its own cost,** which I paid directly. Module 5's key exists, but because it is an `h3` buried inside `## Acceptance evidence` rather than a top-level section like every other key, my first search for it came back empty and I recorded Module 5 as missing a key. A learner doing the same search reaches the same wrong conclusion and either re-derives the answers or files a duplicate defect. Module 5's prose does say the solution "explains the module outcomes, self-assessment, commands, recovery" — but that sentence is easy to read as boilerplate, because the identical promise in Module 2 is not kept.

## Proposed fix

**Primary — add the eight missing keys.** Add a self-assessment key to each of the eight solution files, matching the shape already proven in `solutions/module-01-what-directive-is.md`: one numbered entry per question, the outcome code it checks, a correct answer, and a short "if you answered X instead, here is the distinction you missed" note. That last part is what makes Module 1's key teach rather than just score.

For the five modules whose only solution is a *lab* solution (02, 07, 10, 11 — and 05, already done), the key belongs in that lab solution, because the module already links there. That avoids adding new files and keeps existing navigation correct.

**Secondary — standardize the heading and level.** Pick one spelling (`## Self-assessment key` reads best) and use it as a top-level `##` section in all twelve solutions, including moving Module 5's existing `h3` out of `## Acceptance evidence`. One predictable heading is what makes the key findable without prose promising it.

**Tertiary — close the loop so this cannot silently regress.** Add a maintainer check under `maintainers/CURRICULUM-MAINTENANCE.md` asserting that every module containing `^## Self-assessment` has a matching `^## Self-assessment key` in its linked solution. This is cheap and deterministic — exactly the kind of gate the course itself teaches in Module 11 — and it is the honest fix, since the defect is a *missing* artifact rather than a wrong one. It would also have caught the Module 5 heading drift.

**If the keys are deliberately withheld** for some modules, say so in the module itself and give the learner the alternative: state which rubric row to self-check against and what evidence substitutes for a key. Silence currently reads as an oversight rather than a choice.

## Environment

- Page: all twelve `curriculum/modules/*.md`, `curriculum/README.md`, `solutions/*.md`
- Commit: f465008
- Directive: `@deftai/directive@0.119.2`, engine `@deftai/directive-core@0.119.2`
- OS/shell: macOS Darwin 25.6.0, zsh 5.9
- Found while: completing the Module 2 self-assessment after Lab 2 acceptance passed; corrected while completing Module 5
narratives.UserStory: As a self-directed 3Ci engineer working through the core modules, I want every shipped self-assessment key to sit under one predictable heading and every graded item to name its outcome, so that I can find the key by search and join my answer to the Completion-evidence row that scores it.
narratives.ImplementationPlan:
1. Rename the three non-canonical keys in solutions/module-04-xbrief-as-durable-state.md, solutions/lab-05-projection-drift-recovery.md, and solutions/module-06-creating-well-shaped-work.md to `## Self-assessment key`, promoting the Lab 5 h3 out of `## Acceptance evidence` to h2.
2. In the same change, add `#self-assessment-key` fragment links to the explained-solution close of curriculum modules 04, 05, and 06 — never fragment-link first against the live misspelled or nested headings, which fails the link checker.
3. Tag Module 4 self-assessment items 1-5 to O4.1, O4.2, O4.3, O4.3, O4.4 so each item joins an existing Completion-evidence row.
4. Resolve Module 3 item 5 and Module 6 item 5 as ungraded practice or add a Completion-evidence row; do not tag all seven items uniformly.
5. Wire `scripts/verify-modules-2-3.mjs` into the `test:content` lane in package.json without inventing `scripts/verify-modules-2-3.test.mjs`, then run the module verifiers to confirm the heading renames did not break the shared solution-heading contracts.

items.title: Standardize the four extant keys to `## Self-assessment key`, including promoting Module 5's nested h3 out of Acceptance evidence. Land those heading edits and `#self-assessment-key` fragment links on Modules 4, 5, and 6 in one change. Do not land fragment-link first against the live misspelled or nested headings.

narrative.Acceptance: When a maintainer greps `^## Self-assessment key`, the search returns all four shipped keys, including the former Lab 5 h3 that now renders as an h2 outside `## Acceptance evidence`. The same change adds `#self-assessment-key` fragment links on modules 04, 05, and 06, and the link check emits no broken local heading link.
